issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_make_y_state(...)` (leading underscore) but the template and solution use the name `make_y_state(...)` (no underscore). This name mismatch between the specification and the provided code can confuse students about which function to implement and may cause test harnesses or example code to call a different symbol than the student implements.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either update the problem statement to refer to `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (recommended), or rename the template and solution functions to `_make_y_state(...)` to match the statement. Ensure any tests and docstrings are updated to use the same name.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_make_y_state(...)` (leading underscore), but both the template and the reference solution define the function as `make_y_state(...)` (no leading underscore). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual task (preparing a noisy |Y> state) can confuse students when mapping the task description to the starter code and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name across all artifacts. Either rename the function in the problem statement to `make_y_state(...)` to match the template and solution, or rename the function in the template and solution to `_make_y_state(...)`. Prefer updating the problem statement to `make_y_state(...)` to match common public helper naming and the provided code.
